The current Neurolinguistics entry names Statistics II, the older Psycholinguistics unit and Clinical Linguistics Adults. The developmental language disorders seminar names Clinical Linguistics Children and Statistics II. The 2026–2027 Clinical Linguistics course explicitly changes its own entry from 2027–2028 to Language and Speech Disorders. That prospective update does not establish a replacement rule for the two seminars.

Tested the remaining three formal portfolio choices in OER order as a neutral alternative. Ocasys requires Syntax 2 for Syntax and Phonology 2 for Phonology. Semantics/Pragmatics says either Semantics 2 or Pragmatics, while Part B says both, and the revised course list contains both. The currently dated Syntax 2 listing explicitly names the older stand-alone Syntax 1 code, and Phonology 2 names the older Phonology 1 or an equivalent to discuss with the lecturer. Part B names the new combined foundation, but the dated catalogue does not confirm the revised cohort’s entry treatment. In any event, changing the portfolio does not verify the compulsory project.

The assessment plan confirms the written assignment, poster and presentation structure. The historical accreditation panel describes reductions in portfolio choices and a planned change to Statistics II, but the current 2026–2027 adopted OER supplies the 2026 cohort credit structure. The earlier report does not certify future offerings or entry.
